dedupe_keys.name: onitsha nigeria route optimisation of solid waste collection with a capacitated arc routing heuristic

description: This case study applies a new routing method to refuse collection in Onitsha, a large commercial city in south-eastern Nigeria. T. C. Ogwueleke of the University of Abuja published it in the Journal of Applied Sciences and Environmental Management, an open access African journal (online in 2010). The method is a route first, cluster second heuristic for an extended capacitated arc routing problem on an undirected street network, where the aim is to minimise overall cost, taken as essentially the distance travelled by collection vehicles. The heuristic's routes were compared with Onitsha's existing schedule in terms of cost, time and distance. The article is free to read on African Journals Online under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is the city's collection service. Caveats: street network and demand data are not published separately, and savings are relative to the schedule in use at the time. Adopting the heuristic reduced the number of vehicles needed, cut refuse collection cost by 22.86 percent and cut distance travelled per vehicle per day by 16.31 percent. Simulation uses: a documented saving from arc routing in a developing country city, for calibrating collection cost and fleet size models. Related records: the capacitated waste collection routing data (data-capacitated-waste-collection-routing-p02999) and the Bahía Blanca routing instances (data-bahia-blanca-waste-collection-routing-instances) are routing benchmarks.
